How It Works

How Professional Post-Construction Works

Our post-construction process follows a systematic, six-step protocol designed to maximize pathogen elimination and provide verifiable documentation of results. Every step is performed by trained, background-checked technicians.

1
Phase 1: Rough Clean

Performed while construction is wrapping up. Bulk debris removal (lumber scraps, packaging, drywall pieces), rough sweeping and vacuuming, removal of large protective films and labels, and clearing of trash and recyclables. The goal is making the space safe and accessible for final trades.

2
Phase 2: Detail Clean

Begins after all construction trades have finished. This is the most labor-intensive phase: detailed top-to-bottom dusting, all floor surfaces vacuumed and mopped, interior glass and mirrors cleaned, fixtures and hardware wiped, paint overspray and adhesive residue removed, and HVAC vents and registers cleaned of construction dust.

3
Phase 3: Final Polish

A supervisor walks the entire space with a detailed checklist. Final glass polishing for streak-free windows, spot-checking all surfaces for dust or residue, fixture polishing, final floor care (vacuuming, mopping, or buffing), and verification that all areas are presentation-ready.

4
Punchlist Walk-Through

A formal walk-through with the project manager or building owner identifies any remaining items. Deficiencies are documented and addressed immediately, ensuring sign-off on a complete, move-in ready space.

5
HVAC System Cleaning

Construction dust that has accumulated in ductwork, registers, and HVAC components is removed to prevent distribution throughout the building once systems are activated. Filter replacement ensures the air handling system delivers clean air from day one.

6
Documentation

Before-and-after photos, areas cleaned, hours invested, and any punchlist items are documented in JaniTrack. This documentation serves as proof of completion for general contractors, building owners, and certificate of occupancy inspections.

FAQ

Post-Construction FAQ — Stamford, CT

Common questions about post-construction services in Stamford.

What is post-construction cleanup?+
Post-construction cleanup is the specialized, multi-phase cleaning process that transforms a construction or renovation site into a move-in ready commercial space. It involves three phases: rough cleaning (bulk debris removal), detail cleaning (comprehensive dust elimination from all surfaces and systems), and final cleaning (precision polish and inspection). It requires specialized equipment and expertise beyond standard janitorial capabilities.
What are the three phases of post-construction cleaning?+
Phase 1 (rough clean) removes bulk construction debris, packaging, and large waste while final trades are completing work. Phase 2 (detail clean) is the most labor-intensive — top-to-bottom dust removal, floor cleaning, glass cleaning, fixture detailing, and HVAC vent cleaning. Phase 3 (final polish) is quality assurance — a supervisor inspects every surface with a detailed checklist and addresses any remaining items to achieve move-in ready conditions.
How long does post-construction cleanup take?+
Timeline depends on project size, complexity, and how clean the construction team left the site. A typical 10,000 sq ft office buildout requires 2-3 days for all three phases. A 50,000 sq ft facility may require 1-2 weeks. Healthcare and laboratory spaces take longer due to higher cleanliness standards. We provide a detailed timeline after an initial site assessment.
How much does post-construction cleaning cost?+
Post-construction cleanup typically costs $0.15-$0.50 per square foot depending on project complexity, construction cleanliness, number of floors, and finish types. A standard 10,000 sq ft office buildout ranges from $1,500-$5,000 for all three phases. Medical, laboratory, and highly finished spaces cost more due to elevated standards. Rush timelines carry a 25-50% premium.
Do you handle construction debris removal?+
Yes. We handle complete debris removal including lumber scraps, packaging materials, drywall pieces, protective films, and general construction waste. We coordinate with waste hauling services for dumpster management and ensure proper disposal and recycling of all materials in compliance with local regulations.
Can you work alongside active construction crews?+
Yes. We routinely perform phased cleanup alongside ongoing construction — cleaning completed sections while trades continue work in other areas. We coordinate closely with your general contractor on scheduling, access, and safety protocols to avoid conflicts and maintain project timelines.
Do you clean HVAC systems after construction?+
Yes. Construction dust that accumulates in ductwork, registers, return air grilles, and HVAC components is removed as part of our detail clean phase. We also replace all filters. This step is critical because activating an HVAC system full of construction dust distributes fine particulates throughout the building — creating air quality issues and accelerating equipment wear.
